title: Garnish a full glass of water with a lime wedge: push its slit onto the 2 mm rim without tipping or spilling the glass
instruction: Pick up the lime wedge by its two cut ends, turn it slit-down and push its slit onto the rim of the glass so it sits astride the rim, then let go, without tipping the glass or spilling water.
context: A lime wedge on the rim is how a drink is finished at a bar, a cafe or a party: a short slit is cut into the wedge's flesh and pushed down over the rim, so the wedge sits astride it, half over the drink, and stays. The slit has to be lined up with a rim only 2 mm thick and pushed on hard enough to open the cut (about 1 to 3 N); a wedge dropped on the rim just perches on it or falls in. Meanwhile the glass, a tall highball full of water to 2 cm below the rim, must stay still: pushed sideways at the rim with only about 1.1 N it falls over, and a jolt or a tilt slops water out. The wedge is held only by its two trimmed ends, so the fingers never touch the flesh's juice or the drink, and it must be turned slit-down on the way.
setup: Millimetres from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the counter (the table top). 1) Glass: a Libbey 161 Heavy Base Hi-Ball, 10.25 oz (303 ml to the brim), 133.4 tall, 57.2 across the rim, 63.5 across the base, clear glass, about 200 g (estimate from its shape); wall 2.0 and solid base 11.5 thick (estimates that give the published 303 ml). It stands on a dry sheet of white copy paper (on a thin waterproof plastic table sheet, 50 x 70 cm, so a knocked-over glass cannot wet the rig; neither is modelled) with its base centred at (220, 0) and holds 255 ml of cold tap water, no ice: the surface is 20 below the rim (pour 255 ml from a measuring jug). Glass and water 458 g. 2) Cutting board: a Winco CBWT-610 white polyethylene board, 254 x 152.4 x 12.7, about 0.47 kg, centred at (215, -150), its long side along x. 3) Lime wedge, cut fresh to this recipe (one minute with a paring knife): a Persian lime 48 to 54 across (use 51 if you can choose; the USDA reference lime is 2 in across, 67 g) and about 60 long; trim 5 off each end, halve it lengthwise, cut each half lengthwise into four wedges, then cut a slit 14 deep straight into the middle of a wedge's flesh, across the wedge, from its inner edge toward the peel (half way through). The wedge is 50 long, 25.5 from inner edge to peel, about 8 g. It lies on one cut face on the board with its length along y, the middle of its inner edge at (205, -150), the inner edge toward the robot and the peel away from it. Frictions (estimates): wedge peel and ends 0.5, cut flesh on glass 0.25, glass on paper 0.4, board 0.5. Each gripper pad wears a nitrile finger-cot as a pad cover; the pads touch only the wedge's two trimmed ends. Start: both arms at their ready pose, grippers open. The README lists every collider, joint and mass.
scoring: Judged at the end of the run from the trial video, a photo and a ruler. Seated: the glass wall is inside the slit and the wedge's lowest point is at least 7 mm below the rim's top (ruler stood on the counter against the glass); the wedge rests on the rim on its own, both grippers at least 3 cm from it, and has been still for 1 s. Spilled: in the real trial, any water on the paper or the counter, or running down the outside of the glass; in the simulation, which has no water, the glass tilted more than 10 degrees or moved sideways faster than 0.15 m/s (a jolt) at any time. Knocked over: the glass tilted more than 30 degrees at any time. Score 0: the glass was knocked over, or the wedge was never lifted 3 cm off the board (doing nothing scores 0). 1.0: seated, nothing spilled. 0.75: seated but spilled. 0.5: not seated but resting on the rim on its own and still (for example perched on the slit's mouth, or lying across the rim, its middle within 2 cm of the rim's line), nothing spilled. 0.25: every other outcome once the wedge was lifted: it fell into the drink, onto the board or counter, is still held, or rests on the rim after a spill.
reset_notes: About 2 minutes. Throw the used wedge away and dry the counter. Refill the glass to 255 ml (20 mm below the rim) with cold water, dry its outside, and stand it back at (220, 0) on a fresh dry sheet of white copy paper. Cut a fresh wedge to the recipe in the setup (keep limes in the fridge at about 4 C and cut each wedge no more than 30 minutes before its trial; one lime gives eight wedges) and lay it on one cut face at its start place on the board, inner edge toward the robot. Change the nitrile pad covers when they are wet. If the glass was knocked over, stop the trial, mop the plastic sheet dry and wipe the grippers before the next one. Return both arms to the ready pose.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. No liquid: the water is a solid body in the glass (its mass and centre), so spilling is judged from the glass's tilt (>10 deg) or a jolt (>0.15 m/s). The slit's cut flesh is two sprung plates on 1.3 mm slides (estimates: ~2.7 N peak to open the cut, ~0.7 N to slide on or pull off); the alignment and the push are real. Wedge mass, glass wall and base thickness and mass, and all frictions are estimates; the paper sheet is not modelled.
